# The native app without main.c, the shell and Runtime Upload, for harnesses that drive the real JS thread.
# Benchmark Mode lives in the shipping binary

Performance work targets the Vita, on the device and in Vita3K, where there is no profiler we can script and no command line. So benchmarks run inside the normal VitaDeck build: a `bench/request` file in the VitaDeck Data Root turns on Benchmark Mode for one launch (`src/core/bench.c`). It plays scripted pad input against installed example Deck Apps, keeps timings in preallocated memory, writes `bench/result.json` once at the end, and exits. `scripts/bench.sh` places the request and collects the result: a file on the host and in Vita3K, VitaShell FTP on the device.

Measuring the binary that ships keeps the numbers honest. Off, each hook is a call that returns on its first branch, so normal runs pay nothing measurable. On, a frame costs about ten monotonic clock reads, a JS loop iteration about six, and there is no I/O or logging until the run ends. Per-thread CPU time comes from the OS (`runClocks` on the Vita) and is read twice per scenario.

**Considered options:** a separate benchmark build with a compile-time flag (rejected: a second VPK to build and upload, and it measures a different binary); a CTest harness like the smoke test (rejected: it only runs on the host, and host numbers say little about the Vita); per-frame logging through `TraceLog` (rejected: logging on the Vita is slow enough to skew what it measures); sampling profilers (none for the Vita that we can drive from a script).

**Consequences:** scenarios and their input scripts are C (`SCENARIOS` in `src/core/bench.c`) and drive the example Deck Apps, so changing an example can change a benchmark. Re-record the baseline (`scripts/bench.sh <target> --update-baseline`) when that happens. Vita3K numbers reflect the emulator on the machine that ran it; compare them only against a baseline from the same machine, and treat the device as the source of truth.

diff --git a/src/core/bench.h b/src/core/bench.h
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..bc4cffa
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/core/bench.h
@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+#ifndef VD_BENCH_H
+#define VD_BENCH_H
+
+// Benchmark Mode: plays scripted scenarios against installed Deck Apps, times the frame loop and the JS thread, writes
+// <data root>/bench/result.json and exits. A <data root>/bench/request file turns it on for one launch;
+// scripts/bench.sh writes it. Samples stay in memory until a scenario ends, and when Benchmark Mode is off every hook
+// returns on its first branch.
+
+#include <stdbool.h>
+#include <stdint.h>
+#include "quickjs.h"
+#include "core/js_runtime.h"
+
+// Consecutive spans of a UI frame; each mark ends the span the previous one started.
+typedef enum {
+    VD_BENCH_FRAME_INPUT,   // Shell update and input
+    VD_BENCH_FRAME_BEGIN,   // BeginDrawing and the clear, where vitaGL may wait for the GPU
+    VD_BENCH_FRAME_LAYOUT,  // the render lock, and layout of a new snapshot
+    VD_BENCH_FRAME_GLYPHS,  // caching the frame's glyphs and uploading atlas pages
+    VD_BENCH_FRAME_DRAW,    // walking the instance tree and issuing draw calls
+    VD_BENCH_FRAME_SHELL,   // Shell paint
+    VD_BENCH_FRAME_PRESENT, // EndDrawing: buffer swap, vsync and raylib's frame limiter
+    VD_BENCH_FRAME_SPAN_COUNT,
+} VdBenchFrameSpan;
+
+// Consecutive spans of a JS thread loop iteration.
+typedef enum {
+    VD_BENCH_JS_INPUT,
+    VD_BENCH_JS_TIMERS,
+    VD_BENCH_JS_FETCH,
+    VD_BENCH_JS_MICROTASKS,
+    VD_BENCH_JS_SWAP,
+    VD_BENCH_JS_SPAN_COUNT,
+} VdBenchJsSpan;
+
+// UI thread. Call after package_library_init and before the Active Deck App starts; makes the first scenario's
+// Deck App active when Benchmark Mode is on.
+void bench_init(void);
+bool bench_active(void);
+// UI thread, first thing every frame. Advances the scenario and may ask for a Deck App Runtime Restart. Returns
+// false once every scenario ran and the result is written.
+bool bench_update(const VdJsRuntime *runtime, bool *request_runtime_restart);
+// UI thread, in place of the input polls: applies this frame's scripted pad input.
+void bench_apply_input(void);
+void bench_frame_mark(VdBenchFrameSpan span);
+
+// JS thread.
+void bench_js_thread_start(void);
+void bench_js_ready(void);
+void bench_js_iteration_begin(void);
+void bench_js_mark(VdBenchJsSpan span);
+void bench_js_iteration_end(JSRuntime *rt, bool busy, bool swapped);
+// After each input event's handler returns. A Deck App that cannot keep up handles a backlog in one iteration, so
+// this also opens and closes the window mid-iteration.
+void bench_js_input_handled(JSRuntime *rt, uint64_t queued_us, uint64_t started_us);
+// Brackets a React commit: prepareForCommit to resetAfterCommit.
+void bench_commit(bool ended);
+
+#endif /* VD_BENCH_H */
